changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retailers selling in stores and online, especially when the store-operations lead or COO is in the room: lead with "One system for the tills and the website" and "one customer, one basket". Prove it with a live, step-by-step walkthrough instead of a diagram: an online order returned at a store till, refunded to the original payment method, on the same customer record. Use this in place of the claim that the line between online and in-store has disappeared.
changes.why: Our M3 pitch drew silence and was dismissed as "that's a diagram"; the buyer then asked how a return works step by step at the till, which is the buy-online-return-in-store failure that started the evaluation and is described in the customer's own words.

changes.change: For the COO / store-operations buyer, add an accountability line and proof point: one contract and one team accountable for the tills and the website, including installs, so there are never two vendors pointing at each other. Back it with a rollout plan that covers "Dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills." Where installs go through a partner, state who owns the outcome end to end.
changes.why: The buyer said "I don't want two vendors pointing at each other". Our partner answer on installs ended her questions at the workshop. The customer wanted a rollout plan, and the winning competitor brought people who had done store rollouts on one contract.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For retail store buyers, replace the pointer to customer stories with named retail reference customers who are ready to take a call on short notice, offered alongside the live till-return demo.
changes.why: The buyer asked "can I talk to them?" and we could not set up a call in time. The competitor named retailers the COO knew, and we described the till return instead of showing it.

changes.change: In retail store conversations, say "the tills" instead of "in-person payments" or "point of sale". Talk about one customer across store and web, not product categories.
changes.why: The customer consistently said "the tills" and framed the problem as one system and one customer, while we kept using our category terms.
